newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu, Arafat open U.S.-brokered Hebron summit.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu, Arafat open U.S.-brokered Hebron summit.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat opened a U.S.-brokered summit on Tuesday in a bid to clinch a long-elusive deal on the West Bank town of Hebron.

The two men last met at crisis talks in Washington called by U.S. President Bill Clinton in the aftermath of fierce clashes between Israeli and Palestinian security forces that killed 75 people last September.
U.S. Middle East peace envoy Dennis Ross dampened expectations a deal on an Israeli troop redeployment from Israeli-occupied Hebron could be sealed on Tuesday.

"We have clearly energised negotiations over the last couple of days," Ross told reporters, in a reference to his mediation shuttle that began late on Saturday. But he added: "I don't expect that one meeting is going to conclude this."
Israel and the PLO have accused each other of foot-dragging in nearly three months of talks on Hebron, most of which was due to have been handed over to Palestinian self-rule last March.
Ross said the sides were trying to hammer out "complex" details holding up a final Hebron deal.
Any deal on the town is likely to breathe new life into an Arab-Israeli peace process which only recently appeared on the brink of collapse.

Netanyahu, who came to power in June vowing to take a tough line on Israeli security, has demanded protection for 400 Jewish settlers who live and study in the heart of the city of 100,000 Arabs, a longtime flashpoint of violence between Arabs and Jews.
Arafat seeks Israeli commitments that implementation of interim peace deals he signed with Israel's previous centre-left government will not stop once the Hebron deal is done.
"I believe that we will see, at a time that I can't predict yet, a balanced agreement," Ross said.
